// what this config is for: The PUBLISHED artifact. tsconfig.json typechecks the sources in place; this one emits dist/ — the .js and .d.ts every consumer actually resolves. See README, 'What this package publishes'.
// module note: nodenext, NOT the bundler mode tsconfig.json uses for editing. This is the emit that ships, so it is checked against the strictest resolver a consumer can have — real Node ESM. That is what FORCES every relative import to carry its .js extension: the package is "type": "module", Node does not guess extensions, and bundler mode would happily let an unloadable package out the door because webpack/Vite/Metro do guess.
// sourceMap note: inlineSources embeds the TypeScript in the .map, so a consumer debugging a crash inside <Resource> gets real source WITHOUT this package shipping src/. There is deliberately no declarationMap: it would need src/ on disk to be followable, and src/ is exactly what stopped being published — the .d.ts IS the contract, and is the right place for a consumer's editor to land.
